paragraphs: On Friday afternoon, the school had a sports festival. Lily and Mia were in the swimming race for their class. They went to the school pool at two o'clock. Coach Matt stood at the gate with a silver whistle around his neck. "Stop here, please," he said. "Anyone who wants to swim must read the sign first."

This is what the sign said. "POOL SAFETY" "One: Walk. Do not run." "Two: Check how deep the water is." "Three: Never swim alone." "Four: Do exercise for five minutes before you swim." "Five: Danger! Do not jump near other people." "Six: Stop when you feel ill, and tell Coach Matt." Mia read the sign two times.

"Why do we do exercise before we swim?" asked Mia. "Exercise makes your body warm," said Coach Matt. "A warm body swims better, and it stays healthy." The girls moved their arms and legs on the grass for five minutes. Then Lily put her hand on her heart. "My heart is fast!" she said. "That is normal after exercise," said Coach Matt. "Drink some water and wait for a minute."

Next, Coach Matt took the girls to the side of the pool. "Check the water," he said. The near end of the pool was one meter deep. The far end was two meters deep, and a red line of floats was in the middle. "Stay on this side of the red line," said Coach Matt. "I can swim in deep water," said Mia. "I know," he said, "but today the race is at the near end."

The girls waited for their turn, and they walked on the dry floor. Some children from other classes waited in line, too. Nobody ran, and nobody swam alone. At half past two, Coach Matt used his whistle, and the race began. Lily swam fast, and Mia swam next to her. Both girls smiled at the end of the race, and their friends clapped. Then they dried their hands and their faces with a towel. "The sign helped us," said Lily. "It helps anyone who reads it," said Coach Matt.
